title: Fruit Into Baskets
description:
# Fruit Into Baskets

You are visiting a farm with a single row of fruit trees from left to right. The integer array `fruits` describes the row: `fruits[i]` is the type of fruit produced by the `i`th tree.

You have exactly two baskets:

* Each basket may contain only one fruit type.
* Each basket can hold any number of fruits of its assigned type.
* You may choose any starting tree.
* Starting there, you must pick exactly one fruit from every tree while moving right.
* You must stop before the first tree whose fruit type does not fit in either basket.

Return the maximum number of fruits you can pick.

This is equivalent to finding the longest contiguous subarray containing at most two distinct values.

## Example 1

**Input:** fruits = [1,2,1]
**Output:** 3
**Explanation:** All three trees contain only two fruit types, so the whole row can be collected.

## Example 2

**Input:** fruits = [0,1,2,2]
**Output:** 3
**Explanation:** Starting at the second tree collects [1,2,2]. Starting at the first tree would stop after [0,1].

## Example 3

**Input:** fruits = [1,2,3,2,2]
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The best choice is [2,3,2,2].

## Constraints

* `1 <= fruits.length <= 10^5`
* `0 <= fruits[i] < fruits.length`

tests.description: All trees fit in two baskets
Best window starts after the first tree
Third type forces the start to move
Classic case with a long middle window
Exactly two fruit types across the whole row
Every third tree forces a reset
Best window is a run of two adjacent types
Best window keeps a repeated non-adjacent pair
Third type appears before a long suffix window
Best answer begins after two early distinct types

solutions.name: Sliding Window with HashMap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Treat the two baskets as the condition "the current subarray may contain at most two distinct fruit types." Expand the right boundary one tree at a time, store fruit counts in a HashMap, and shrink the left boundary while the map contains more than two keys.

## Key Insight

The HashMap size is the number of basket types currently in use. Counts are needed because a fruit type should leave the map only after every copy of that type has moved out of the window.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the map holds at most three fruit types before shrinking

solutions.name: Sliding Window with Bounded Count Array
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the prompt constraint `0 <= fruits[i] < fruits.length` to replace the HashMap with an integer count array indexed by fruit type. Maintain a distinct counter and shrink the same sliding window whenever that counter becomes three.

## Key Insight

This route teaches the same invariant as the HashMap solution but makes the value-range tradeoff explicit: direct indexing is simple and fast only because the prompt bounds fruit type ids.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n), for the type-count array allowed by the value range

solutions.name: Last Seen Eviction
solutions.description:
## Approach

Track the last index where each fruit type appears inside the current window. When a third type appears, evict the type whose last occurrence is farthest left, then jump the window start just after that index.

## Key Insight

The evicted type cannot remain in any valid window ending at the current tree, because its last copy is before both remaining types. This turns repeated left-shrinking into one explanatory jump.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), with only up to three entries scanned on each eviction
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only a constant number of fruit types are tracked

solutions.name: Last Run Constant Space
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep only two active fruit types, the length of the current valid window, and the length of the final consecutive run of the most recent type. If a third type arrives, the new window is exactly the previous final run plus the new tree.

## Key Insight

After a third type appears, every older tree before the final run must be discarded. The final run is the only part of the previous window that can still pair with the new fruit type.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Quadratic Distinct-Type Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Try every starting tree, extend right while collecting fruit types in a set, and stop that start as soon as a third type appears. Record the longest valid segment encountered.

## Key Insight

This baseline follows the prompt literally: choose a start, move right, and stop when the baskets cannot fit the next fruit. It is too slow for the full constraint but useful as the definition-level model.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the set never needs to hold more than three types before breaking
